## About this guide

> Load a metadata snapshot, inspect its relationships and extract metadata from your own PostgreSQL database.

Read the [Terminology](terminology.html) and find the example files in [Package resources](resources.html).

## Load the example metadata

The snapshot models the `form.model` survey form and the reference tables supplied by `form.references`.

```{r metadata}
# Load the metadata and model functions.
library(db.atlas)
# Locate the example snapshot installed with the package.
metadata_directory <- system.file("examples", "survey", "metadata", package = "db.atlas")
# Read the schema, table, column and key metadata.
schema_metadata <- read_metadata(metadata_directory)
# Build an in-memory model of the schemas and relationships.
schema_model <- build_schema_model(schema_metadata)
```

## Inspect dependencies

A dependency records which table holds the foreign key and which table it references.

```{r dependencies}
# Read the model's foreign key relationships.
schema_dependencies <- model_dependencies(schema_model)
# Display the source table, foreign key and target table.
schema_dependencies[, c("table_id", "foreign_key", "target_table_id"), with = FALSE]
```

`survey.observations` references the station and observer catalogues.

`survey.samples` references observations by station and observation ID.

Use [Schema reports](reports.html) to render the model as an HTML atlas with a dependency graph.

## Extract a snapshot from PostgreSQL

Supply a zero-argument function that opens a DBI connection. Extraction closes the connection when it finishes.

This example uses the RPostgres driver and reads the connection settings from the environment.

```{r extract-metadata, eval=FALSE}
# Create a provider that opens a fresh connection when extraction starts.
connection_provider <- function() {
  # Use the application's PostgreSQL settings.
  DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), dbname = Sys.getenv("PGDATABASE"))
}
# Extract the chosen schemas.
schema_metadata <- extract_schema_metadata(c("survey", "catalogue"), connection_provider)
# Save the metadata in an application-selected directory for offline use.
write_metadata(schema_metadata, "metadata-snapshot")
```

Pass the snapshot directory to `read_metadata()` to build a model in a later session.
